transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because of what’s been going on at my apartment building. It’s been… it’s been bothering me a lot. I know the people there are watching when I leave and when I come back, like they’re keeping track of my comings and goings. And there are these notes, and I’m sure they’re slipping them to the office about me.

Everybody keeps saying, “Oh, those are just notices on the doors,” like regular building notices, but that’s not what it feels like to me. It feels like they’re about me, or because of me, and like people are acting like I’m not supposed to notice. I’ve tried to ignore it, but it keeps happening, and I can’t just pretend I don’t see the pattern. So that’s why I’m here, because I need somebody to understand what’s actually going on.
When you see these notes or notices, do you feel that they are specifically meant for you, even if others say they are for everyone?

Yes. I mean, that’s what I’ve been trying to explain. They might look like regular notices to everybody else, like something taped up or put on the door, but when I see them, I can tell there’s more to it. It’s the timing, and the way people act around it, and how it happens after I come or go from the building.

People keep saying, “No, that’s for everyone,” but I don’t think they’re seeing what I’m seeing. It feels like those notes are connected to me, like they’re about what I’m doing, or like somebody’s putting them there because of me. And then I think they’re taking information about me to the office too, like slipping notes in or reporting things. It’s not just a piece of paper to me. It feels directed at me.
Have you noticed any other situations outside of your apartment building where you felt things were directed at you or had a special meaning for you?

Mostly it’s the apartment building. That’s the main place I’ve noticed it, and that’s why I came in. I don’t want to start saying it’s everywhere if I’m not sure, but at the building it’s pretty clear to me.

It’s like, I leave, I come back, and then there’s a notice or a note, and people act like it’s nothing, like it’s just for everybody. But I can tell by the timing and how they behave that it’s got something to do with me. And I keep thinking they’re slipping notes about me to the office, like keeping track of when I go out and when I return.

So outside the apartment building… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it the same way. It’s really the people there and the office and those notices on the doors that feel directed at me.
Have you ever felt that things happening around you—like things people say, events, or objects—have a special meaning or are directed at you, even when others don't see it that way?

Yes, that’s pretty much what I mean. Like I said, it’s mostly at my apartment building, but it’s not just me being sensitive or something. I’ll leave the building, or I’ll come back in, and then there’ll be one of those notices on the door or near the office, and everybody acts like it’s just some regular paper for all the tenants. But to me, the timing is too exact.

It feels like it’s connected to what I’m doing. Like they’re watching when I go out and when I return, and then somebody is putting those notes up or slipping information to the office about me. People say, “No, that’s just a notice,” but I don’t see it that way. It feels directed at me, like there’s a message in it or like it’s happening because of me.

And it makes me feel uncomfortable, because when other people brush it off, it’s like they’re not seeing the whole thing. I know what it looks like from the outside, but when you’re the one living there and it keeps lining up that way, it doesn’t feel random.
When you see these notices or notes in your building, do you believe they are communicating a hidden message meant specifically for you, even though others might not see it that way?

Yes, I do. I mean, I know other people say, “It’s just a notice on the door,” or “Everybody got that,” but that’s not how it feels when I’m the one living there and seeing how it happens.

The reason I came in is because I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and when I come back. It’s like my comings and goings are being tracked, and then these notes show up, or I feel like they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it’s nothing, just regular building notices, but to me it feels like there’s something behind it, like it’s meant for me or about me.

It’s not just the paper itself. It’s the timing, where it’s put, how people act around it. That’s what makes it seem like there’s a message there, even if nobody else admits it.

When you see these notices or notes, do you believe that they are meant only for you and that they carry a special message that others wouldn’t understand, even if the same notice is posted for everyone?

Yes… yes, that’s what it feels like to me. I know you’re saying even if it’s posted for everyone, and that’s the part people keep using against me, like, “See, it’s on everyone’s door,” or “It’s just a building notice.” But I don’t think that explains the timing of it.

I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and when I come back. It’s not just one time. It’s like my comings and goings are being paid attention to, and then these notes or notices show up, and I feel like they’re slipping notes about me to the office too. Like they’re keeping track, but making it look normal.

So yes, I do think there’s something in it meant for me, even if the paper looks like it’s for everybody. Other people might not understand it because they’re not the one being watched like that. But when I’m the one seeing it happen over and over, it feels personal.
Have you ever felt that events or things happening around you outside of your apartment building were specifically related to you or carried a special meaning for you?

Outside the building… I don’t know, not really in the same way. I mean, I notice things sometimes, but the thing that really stands out, the reason I came in, is what’s happening at my apartment.

That’s where I know people are watching when I leave and when I come back. It’s like my comings and goings are being kept track of, and then these notices show up on the doors or near the office, and everybody keeps saying, “It’s just a regular notice,” like I’m making too much of it. But it doesn’t feel regular to me, because the timing lines up too much.

And it’s not only the notices, either. I feel like people there are slipping notes about me to the office, like they’re reporting on me but doing it in a way that looks normal to everyone else. So outside of the apartment building, I can’t really say it happens like that. It’s mainly there, where I live, and that’s why it bothers me so much.
Do you ever feel that things outside of your apartment building, like things you see or hear, are connected to you or have a special meaning for you, even if it's not as clear as in your building?

Maybe a little, but not like at the apartment. I don’t want to make it sound like every single thing outside is about me, because that’s not really what I’m trying to say. The main thing is where I live. That’s where it’s happening the strongest.

I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and when I come back. Like, I’ll go out, and then later there’s a notice on the door, or something by the office, and everybody acts like it’s just regular building stuff. But to me it feels connected. It’s the timing of it. It’s how it shows up after I’ve been in and out. And I feel like people there are slipping notes about me to the office, like they’re reporting on me but doing it in this quiet way so it just looks normal.

Outside the building, I might notice things sometimes and wonder for a second, but it doesn’t have the same pattern. At the apartment, it’s over and over, and that’s why I can’t just brush it off like everyone keeps telling me to.

Do you ever feel that random events or objects, like something on TV or a conversation you overhear, are secretly about you or meant for you, even if they don’t seem connected to your apartment building?

Not really like TV or random conversations, no… I mean, I can get uneasy, but the thing I keep trying to explain is it’s at my apartment. That’s where it’s clear to me.

I came in because I know the people there are watching when I leave and when I come back. It’s not just me seeing something on television and thinking, “Oh, that’s about me.” It’s more like I step out, I come back, and then there’s a notice on the door or something around the office, and everybody says, “That’s just a regular notice, everybody got one.” But that doesn’t explain why it keeps lining up with me like that.

And I feel like people are slipping notes about me to the office too, like they’re reporting on my comings and goings, but doing it in a way where if I say something, I look like I’m overreacting. So if you’re asking about outside things, random things, I don’t know that I’d say that. It’s mainly the apartment and those notices and the way people act like it’s nothing.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others around you didn’t seem to notice or agree with, even when there was no clear evidence to support your belief?

Yes… yes, that’s basically what I’ve been trying to say. I know other people don’t agree with me about it, and they keep acting like I’m reading too much into it, but I can’t just ignore it.

At my apartment, I know people are watching when I leave and when I come back. I’ll go out, or I’ll come back in, and then there are these notices on the doors or near the office, and everyone says, “That’s just a normal notice, everybody gets those,” but it doesn’t feel like that to me. The timing is too much. It feels like they’re keeping track of me and then making it look like regular building business.

And I also feel like people are slipping notes about me to the office, like they’re reporting on my comings and goings, but doing it quietly so nobody else sees it the way I do. That’s the part that bothers me, because if I say something, they just look at me like I’m imagining it. But to me it’s not just nothing. It’s been happening enough that I came in here because I need someone to understand what I’m talking about.

Do you believe, without any doubt, that the notices and behaviors of others in your apartment building are directed at you and meant to communicate something specific about you, even though others have told you they are just regular building notices and there’s no proof otherwise?

Yes… I mean, I know how that sounds when you say “without any doubt,” but yes, that’s why I came in. Because to me it’s not just regular notices on the doors. Everybody keeps telling me, “No, that’s just building notices, that’s just the office doing their job,” but I know the people in that apartment building are watching when I leave and when I come back.

It’s the way it happens. I go out, I come back, and then there’s something posted, or something near the office, or people are acting like they know something. And I feel like they’re slipping notes about me to the office, like reporting on my comings and goings, but doing it in a way where if I try to point it out, they can just say I don’t have proof.

So yes, I believe it’s directed at me. Maybe not every single paper in the whole building, but the pattern, the timing, the way people act around it — that’s what makes me know it’s about me.

doctor.question: Do you believe, without any doubt, that the notices and behaviors of others in your apartment building are directed at you and meant to communicate something specific about you, even though others have told you they are just regular building notices and there’s no proof otherwise?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me to the office, even though everybody keeps telling me it's just notices on the doors.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a fixed belief that apartment notices and others’ behaviors are directed at the patient despite others saying they are ordinary and without proof, which directly matches delusions.

patient.answer:
Yes… I mean, I know how that sounds when you say “without any doubt,” but yes, that’s why I came in. Because to me it’s not just regular notices on the doors. Everybody keeps telling me, “No, that’s just building notices, that’s just the office doing their job,” but I know the people in that apartment building are watching when I leave and when I come back.

It’s the way it happens. I go out, I come back, and then there’s something posted, or something near the office, or people are acting like they know something. And I feel like they’re slipping notes about me to the office, like reporting on my comings and goings, but doing it in a way where if I try to point it out, they can just say I don’t have proof.

So yes, I believe it’s directed at me. Maybe not every single paper in the whole building, but the pattern, the timing, the way people act around it — that’s what makes me know it’s about me.

inference.note: The patient's delusional beliefs are focused on a specific theme—being watched and having notices directed at them in their apartment building. The delusions are non-bizarre, persistent, and limited to this specific context without broader psychotic features or other symptom clusters ruling out F20.0 and F23.0. This is consistent with delusional disorder (F22.0).
